ex: We shall be looking for an improvement in your work this term.
我们期待你这学期功课有进步。

en: to be thinking with pleasure about something that is going to happen (because you expect to enjoy it)
ex: I'm looking forward to the weekend.
我盼着过周末呢。

zh: （尤指当某人生病或需要帮助时到其住处）短暂探访
en: to make a short visit to a place, especially somebody’s house when they are ill or need help
ex: She looks in on her elderly neighbour every evening.
她每天晚上都要看望一下年长的邻居。

en: to examine something
ex: A working party has been set up to look into the problem.
已成立一个工作小组来调查这个问题。

en: to watch something without becoming involved in it yourself
ex: Passers-by simply looked on as he was attacked.
他遭人袭击，路人只在一边袖手旁观。

en: to consider somebody/something to be somebody/something
ex: She's looked on as the leading authority on the subject.
她被视为这门学科的最重要的权威。

en: to consider somebody/something in a particular way
ex: They looked on his behaviour with contempt.
他们对他的行为不屑一顾。

zh: （表示警告，尤指有危险）小心，当心，留神
en: used to warn somebody to be careful, especially when there is danger
ex: Look out! There's a car coming.
当心！有车来了。

zh: 只考虑某人／自己的利益
en: to take care of somebody and make sure nothing bad happens to them
ex: You should look out for pickpockets.
你应当提防扒手。

en: to examine something to see how good, big, etc. it is
ex: We looked over the house again before we decided we would rent it.
那房子我们再看了一次才决定租下来。

en: to turn your head so that you can see something
ex: People came out of their houses and looked around.
人们走出家门四处察看。

en: to search for something in a number of different places
ex: We're looking around for a house in this area.
我们正在这个地区四处找住房。

zh: 佯装没有看见而不理会某人
en: to ignore somebody by pretending not to see them
ex: She just looked straight through me.
她竟然假装没看见我。
